precedence: A project may declare grants and may add its own forbid rules.
Rules forbidden here always override a project grant.

A project may not grant access to any path listed in policyFiles, which is why the project capability file is itself listed there: an agent must not be able to widen its own authority by granting itself write access to the file that records its authority.

That file is exempt from the commit hook, because a project cannot install this policy without committing the grants it declares. Widening is restrained instead by the write deny in generated agent configuration and by server-side code ownership on the policy paths. A commit hook cannot tell a human from an agent, so refusing the commit only obstructed the human the rule was written to serve.
Tightening is always permitted. Widening beyond what this specification allows is not.

grantKinds.tool: Names commands an agent may invoke, matched as a prefix. Optionally declares 'entrypoint', one of the project's own scripts the command runs, and 'mutates', whether the task changes anything outside the repository. Declares intent; it does not install anything or confer operating-system permission.
grantKinds.path: Names filesystem locations an agent may reach, with 'access' of 'read' or 'write'. Declares intent; the operating system is what actually enforces it.
grantKinds.mcp: Names Model Context Protocol tools an agent may call, each written in full as 'mcp__<server>__<tool>'. Any other shape is rejected, because the name reaches the generated allow list verbatim.

forbid.description: Agents must never push directly to a protected branch. Changes reach a protected branch only through a pull request merged by a human.
History rewriting on an agent's own branch is permitted, but only through --force-with-lease.
Agents must not commit to, merge into, reset, or rewrite a protected branch locally.
Centrally managed policy infrastructure changes originate from the policy repository and arrive through synchronization, unless policy mutation is authorized.
Agents configure a repository-local identity only, and must not alter the user's global Git configuration.

sandbox.networkAccessJustification: Agents require network access for 'git fetch', 'git push' of their own branches, and GitHub operations through 'gh'.

enforcementNotes.summary: Generated agent configuration fails fast on the common literal forms of a prohibited action. The Git hooks evaluate the actual refs being pushed and are therefore phrasing-independent. Neither layer constrains an agent that deliberately bypasses it; server-side branch protection is the only boundary an agent does not control.
